# CityMETER · ศูนย์การค้า (Shopping centers)

> Qualified retail venues of Thailand — shopping centres, community malls, outlets, markets, fuel stations with shops, host stores and retail inside projects — counted under one definition, by district (เขต/อำเภอ), with operators, the shops their lists name, their buildings and the straight-line distance to rail stations (CityMETER Transit). A Landometer CityMETER public research demo, release 0.1.28 (2026-11-08). Research master export 2026-11-07 23:55 ICT, with 12 cells of 01_VENUES written and read back on 2026-11-08 (D41).

What one figure means:
- venues (แห่ง) = qualified, countable venues of the research master: several consumer businesses with one common area manager, by source evidence or by a category rule the data owner accepted (the venue panel says which). A parent complex never adds its components. Records still awaiting the definition check, or whose check closed unconfirmed, are grey context dots and never counted. Not a census; not footfall, sales, rent, vacancy, occupancy or market share.
- shops inside (ร้านข้างใน) = branches/listings that 25 registry shop datasets list for a venue, one entry per branch, plus the entries of the centre's own official directory that no brand dataset lists yet (D38, 0.1.27: one name on one floor and unit; brand counters inside department stores, facilities, events and coming-soon rows left out). A venue without a list reads "—", never 0; a shop missing from a list is not shown to be absent; a directory entry is a listed name, not a verified open shop or a legal tenant, and is not in brand search until its brand is linked. A place with sub-areas (a block, a complex) also lists its sub-areas' shops, each naming its sub-area, and counts them once (D41, 0.1.28). Brands with a counter inside a centre's department store are a separate list (แบรนด์ในห้างสรรพสินค้า, D40, 0.1.28), never shops.
- density (แห่ง/ตร.กม.) = venues per km² of the district area of CityMETER production (RTSD 2019 boundaries, production codes).
- distances = straight lines between reference points (haversine), not walking routes or catchments; stations are operating stations only (construction stations are projects, not services).
- size (GLA/GFA) appears only in a venue's own panel; legacy estimates never enter rankings, totals or filters.
- sites = one interior point per building of a multi-building venue (392 venues, 5,743 buildings), mostly from OpenStreetMap areas checked with fixed rules (© OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL 1.0); a site is not a land title, a deed area or ownership.
- type groups = the kind of place a user meets (shopping centre, community mall, outlet, market, host store, fuel, retail inside a project); a retail area typed as part of a project but with a name of its own and no qualified parent reads as the place it is (D36, 0.1.23: Chamchuri Square and Park Silom as shopping centres); a counted retail precinct whose sub-areas are shopping centres shows with them (D41, 0.1.28: Siam Square, whose sub-areas Siam Square One, Siam Scape and Centerpoint no longer count on their own); the registry's own type stays in the venue panel.
- 3D buildings = OpenStreetMap first everywhere (building parts, the outline as the podium under them), CityMETER Building V4 only where OpenStreetMap has no building (D35, 0.1.22); heights are OSM tags or CityMETER model estimates, not surveys.

- next steps in Google (venue panel, D37, 0.1.25) = links to Google AI Mode (a question written for tenants, leasing teams and investors about this exact place), Google Maps (search by name and area) and Street View (a viewpoint on the road in front of the building, facing it). What Google returns — answers, photos, reviews, imagery — is Google's, not CityMETER evidence, and never enters a figure.
Snapshot (release 0.1.28; fixtures, recompute from data):
- 11,139 registry rows; 6,265 qualified; 6,159 countable; 6,153 open or awaiting status, 4 planned, 2 closed; 6,137 located in 733 districts of 77 provinces; 12 of the open or awaiting venues have no point yet (29 placed at owner-identified points in 0.1.27, not field-verified).
- First finding (owner decision D33): 24% of Bangkok's shopping centres, community malls and outlets (57 of 238) are in Pathum Wan, Watthana and Khlong Toei, on 2.2% of its area; 65% of the 57 lie within 500 m of an operating rail station, against 38% (69 of 181) elsewhere in Bangkok. Bangkok holds 678 more places of the other types (D39).
- Shop lists (0.1.28): 22,176 entries at 639 venues = 7,218 brand-dataset listings + 14,958 centre-directory entries at 65 centres (export of 18_OFFICIAL_TENANTS, 26,955 rows: 15,154 shown, 3,161 already listed, 7,735 shown as 7,268 department-store brands at 18 centres, 905 held). Siam Square lists 42 (its own 13 + Siam Square One 27 + Siam Scape 2). The 53 venues of the owner's 7 Nov table: 3,908 listed in 0.1.25, 16,391 now. Brand dataset part: 7,218 displayed listings at 639 hosts from25datasets,1,010 display/search brand-concept keys. All7,108 preceding identities/facts retained;110new listings/16exact-ID corroborations. Six One Bangkok component items are presented once at their retail parent with native child IDs retained. Park Silom23/Central Park64/One Bangkok97. True Digital Park122/17 unchanged. Exact source-to-public coverage audit reads11,139 native inventory rows/26,955 directory observations/211,203 source-link rows;1,129 accepted links still need eligibility review. These populations are not a national physical-tenant census.
- CHAGEE Chamchuri Square and Samyan Mitrtown are distinct branch-host links. Samyan current-open state is owner-reported on 2026-11-07; official locator identity and field operation are separate.
- Native directory research: 26,955 publisher observations at 68 native host IDs / 66 publication groups; source availability queue covers all 11,139 registry rows. Neither a source observation nor an HTTP check is a verified physical outlet.
- Original 31 retail-point audits: 23 selected source-qualified retail/tenant reference points, 8 held without an acceptable point; count roles and venue qualification preserved.
- Every type ranked by count: Mueang Chiang Mai has the most (103, mostly markets).

Deep links (https://montri-th.github.io/shoppingcenter/):
- default type set = centres (mall, community, outlet) · ?group=all — every type · ?group={centres|mall|community|outlet|market|hoststore|component|fuel|other}
- ?province={code} — production codes, e.g. BKK, CMI · ?district={code} — e.g. 1007 (เขตปทุมวัน) · ?areas={code},{code} | ?areas=all
- ?venue={venue id} · ?station={CityMETER Transit station id, e.g. RAILCAT:BTS_SUKHUMVIT:CEN} · ?brand={brand key} · ?record={registry id of a context record}
- ?q={text} · ?status={planned|closed|all} · ?operator={group id|__other__|__none__} · ?role={shop role or facility} · ?view={rank|mix|operators} · ?view3d=0 · ?pending=0

Data and method:
- [Product statement](https://montri-th.github.io/shoppingcenter/PRODUCT_STATEMENT.md): users, problem, decisions, red team (§10)
- [Data and method](https://montri-th.github.io/shoppingcenter/DATA_METHOD.md): definition, counting, first finding, stations, sites, limits
- [Venues](https://montri-th.github.io/shoppingcenter/data/venues.json): rows + meta (definitions, counts, checks.firstView)
- [Rail stations](https://montri-th.github.io/shoppingcenter/data/stations.json) · [Sites](https://montri-th.github.io/shoppingcenter/data/venue-sites.json) · [Shop-list index](https://montri-th.github.io/shoppingcenter/data/tenant-index.json)

Do not claim from this data: footfall, sales, rent, vacancy, occupancy, market share, a market gap or a "golden location", that a venue is open today, walking time, that being near a station causes visits or sales, that a district without venues has none, that a shop not in a list is absent, or that a building height is measured (CityMETER heights are model estimates).
